claims.statement: DeepAgentsServer exposes ACP over newline-delimited JSON on stdin and stdout by wrapping the streams with ndJsonStream and AgentSideConnection; start waits for the connection and reserves protocol traffic for stdout.

The initialize handler negotiates the requested protocol version, returns server identity and capabilities for session loading, images, embedded context, modes, and commands, records client filesystem and terminal capabilities, and advertises configured or default authentication methods.

Each session/new request creates a sess_-prefixed session ID and a separate LangGraph thread ID, selects the requested configOptions.agent or the first configured agent, rejects unknown agents, stores session metadata, lazily creates the selected agent, and advertises built-in plus agent-specific commands.

ACP prompts are converted into LangChain HumanMessage content, streamed through the selected DeepAgent with configurable thread_id and an abort signal, and translated from graph message updates into agent message chunks, thought chunks, and tool completion updates.

Tool-call notifications classify built-in tools by ACP kind, include raw input, formatted titles, and follow-along file locations for path-bearing tools; completed tool updates include textual content and output.
Todo events from the agent are translated into ACP plan updates with medium as the default priority and cancelled todo status mapped to skipped.

The ACP server requests client permission for every observed AI tool call, offers allow-once, allow-always, reject-once, and reject-always options, caches only always decisions per session and tool name, and allows the tool when the permission RPC fails.

When both client filesystem capabilities are advertised and no custom backend is configured, the server uses ACPFilesystemBackend for reads and writes; individual ACP failures fall back to local filesystem operations, while ls, glob, and grep remain local.

ACPFilesystemBackend passes the current session ID and absolute workspace-rooted paths to client file operations, preserves paginated read metadata, and caches one mutable backend per agent rather than one backend per session.

The server has an executeWithTerminal helper that creates /bin/bash -c in the client terminal, waits for exit, collects output, releases the terminal, and returns an error result on terminal failure, but the normal streamAgentResponse path does not dispatch execute calls through it.

All configured agents share a server-created in-memory MemorySaver, and prompts use each session's thread_id; session/load reads checkpoint channel_values.messages and replays user messages, string agent messages, and completed tool calls.

Session persistence is process-local: session/load first requires the session to exist in the in-memory sessions map, stop clears that map, and the default MemorySaver is not durable across process restart; /clear replaces the thread ID to start a fresh checkpoint thread.

Cancellation is controlled by one server-level AbortController: session/cancel aborts the current prompt without matching the notification session ID, and the stream marks active tool calls cancelled before returning a cancelled stop reason.

The server exposes agent, plan, and ask modes and supports set_mode plus slash-command updates, but the current implementation stores the mode without passing it into agent.stream or enforcing read-only tool behavior.

Authentication is advertisement-only: initialize returns default Anthropic and OpenAI env-var methods plus a generic setup method unless authMethods is supplied, while authenticate is a no-op and does not validate credentials.

The logger writes diagnostics to stderr and optional timestamped file output, never normal logs to stdout, preserving stdout for ACP protocol traffic; the CLI supports debug and file logging through flags and environment variables.
start rejects duplicate starts, installs SIGINT and SIGTERM shutdown handlers, handles connection closure and process errors, while stop drops the connection, clears sessions, and closes the logger.

The focused ACP tests exercise real stdio CLI protocol behavior, session and mode routing, cancellation, auth and command responses, message and tool translation, permission decisions, terminal helper behavior, filesystem fallbacks, and adapter conversions.
